title: post_reel.py account-guard line citations (117-118 / 107) are stale; actual lines are 104-105 / 94
description: Both documents cite `post_reel.py:117-118` as the account-guard comparison (`active = ev(...)` at line 117, `if active != a.handle:` at line 118), and claim line 107 is 'the unrelated "not logged in" check'. Fresh re-read of the real file (/Users/anicca/anicca-project/.claude/skills/ig-reels-poster/scripts/post_reel.py, 197 lines total) right now shows: `active = ev(...)` is actually at line 104, `if active != a.handle:` is at line 105, and line 107 is `res["active_account"] = active; print(json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False)); return` — part of the SAME account-guard error-return block, not an unrelated check. The real 'not logged in' check is a distinct string at line 94 (`res["error"] = "not logged in"; print(json.dumps(res)); return`), not line 107. This is the third instance of this spec's specific failure mode (wrong/stale line-number or enumerated-content citations that were not caught by a prior review round) after iteration-1's launch_clip_browser.py path issue and iteration-4's plist 10-vs-4-key issue.
why_not_blocking: The actual CODE PATTERN this citation exists to support — an `active = ev(...)` JS-read followed by `if active != a.handle:` fail-closed account-guard compare, gating on a querySelector against the profile-photo alt text — IS genuinely present and correct in the real file (verified verbatim, git log confirms it was added deliberately: commit 200bc84a 'add ACCOUNT GUARD'). REQ-104/PROP-104's operative instruction ('confirm login via the SAME account-guard check pattern already uses') remains implementable and correct regardless of the specific line numbers cited — an implementer verifying this would grep for the pattern text, not blindly trust a line number. This is the same class of issue iteration-4's FIND-011 ruled non-blocking ('content of each claim was otherwise accurate'), so is scored consistently as informational here.
recommended_fix: Update REQ-104 and PROP-104 to cite `post_reel.py:104-105` (active-handle compare) and note the real 'not logged in' check is at line 94, not 107. Given this is the THIRD recurrence of this exact citation-drift failure mode in this spec's review history, recommend the next implementer treat EVERY specific file:line citation in this spec as a pointer to re-verify via grep at implementation time, not a fact to trust — this matches REQ-106's own already-adopted framing ('the mechanism matters, not a memorized snapshot') and should probably be applied as a blanket caveat across the whole spec rather than fixed line-by-line yet again.
verified_by: Direct re-read of /Users/anicca/anicca-project/.claude/skills/ig-reels-poster/scripts/post_reel.py lines 94-107 and awk-based line-number extraction on 2026-07-04, independent of any prior iteration's citations.
